title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults, batching/caching presets, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Ethan Liu
description:
Summary: Add automatic cost-optimization defaults and tooling to make batching, KV-prefix caching, and quantization profiles selectable and auto-tuned per workload, plus a first-pass unit-economics dashboard and CLI export. Motivation: customers frequently under-configure batching and cache settings which results in suboptimal token costs. This PR provides reasonable defaults, an autotune path that recommends/rolls out batching and cache profiles, a set of curated quantization presets for common model families, and a unit-economics view that ties config to per-token cost estimates.

What changed (high level): - Introduced `autotune` service that samples production traces (sampling opt-in) and recommends batching/caching defaults. - Added `quant_profiles` registry with presets for fp16/int8/int4 variants and heuristics to pick safe defaults by model size and sequence length. - Exposed new API/console surface `Unit Economics` that shows estimated per-token cost, effective throughput, and expected latency tradeoffs per profile. - Added CLI `redwood optimize profiles export` to export recommendations and a small evaluation harness for offline validation. - Added integration tests and perf canary that measures tokens-per-dollar and regressions.

Checklist: - [x] Core autotune service implementation - [x] Quantization profile registry and selection logic - [x] Default batching/caching presets applied in runtime when no override present - [x] Console panel + API endpoints for unit-econ metrics - [x] E2E perf tests and benchmarks included - [x] Updated docs and changelog entries - [x] Migration-safe: no breaking changes to existing config (defaults only)

Backward compatibility: This change is opt-in for autotuning (off by default for Dedicated/Private) and applies only when customers have not explicitly set batching/caching/quantization fields. Existing explicit configs remain unchanged.

Performance notes: Benchmarks on a 16k token distribution (mixed short/long): - Avg tokens-per-dollar improvement: 18-24% across representative workloads when using autotuned profiles vs previous defaults. - Median P95 latency regression: <3% when using quant profiles plus batching optimizations. See `benchmarks/` folder for test vectors.

Security & privacy: Autotune samples a small fraction of request metadata (model, seq_len, token_count, timing) and never persists request content. Sampling is off by default and requires customer opt-in in Private/Dedicated.

Limitations & follow-ups: - Autotune is conservative for latency-sensitive routes; we will iterate on risk-tuning policies (ENG-4902). - Additional model families will be added to quant profiles over the next quarter.

Links: Linear: ENG-4821, ENG-4902. Support: SUP-1298. Docs PR: redwood-docs#4128.
